messages:
jess: Heads-up: saw a 25% p99 regression on yesterday's canary. nsys timeline shows flash_attention_fused_v2 spiking and a KV read stall. dumped a microtrace and nvprof run.

nate: ouch. any quick repro steps?

jess: yep — repro on local dedicated with seed=42 and batch=8. command i used:
```bash
nsys profile -o trace.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none ./run_infer --model=redwood-v1 --batch=8
```

jess: quick filtered timeline from the .nsys capture (trimmed):
```text
[0.00s] flash_attention_fused_v2  kernel  (SMs: 80)  14.2ms
[0.02s] kv_read_kernel            kernel  (SMs: 28)   9.8ms  <- serialized reads
[0.03s] flash_prefetch_shim      kernel  (SMs: 80)   1.1ms
[0.04s] kv_write_kernel           kernel  (SMs: 10)   6.7ms  <- backpressure
```

sara: those kv_read timings look high for batch=8. do you see fan-in from multiple warps hitting the same bank? could be a prefetch stride mismatch between the fused kernel and the KV layout.

jess: exactly. the sampler shows many short read bursts at offsets aligned to 512B boundaries. suspect prefetch stride vs banking -> lots of small scatter reads that serialize on a tiny set of SMs.

perf-bot: Regression alert: canary 2025-03-12 03:21 UTC, p99 latency +24%, top contributors: flash_attention_fused_v2, kv_write_kernel. See /perf/reports/2050012345

nate: can you paste the kernel launch params (grid/block/shared/regs)?

jess: pasted below:
```text
flash_attention_fused_v2 <<<grid=2048,block=128>>> shared=48KB  regs=64
kv_read_kernel            <<<grid=1024,block=64>>>  shared=12KB  regs=32
kv_write_kernel           <<<grid=256,block=128>>>  shared=8KB   regs=28
```

sara: that grid mapping explains SM contention. the fused flash kernel is occupying most SMs and is prefetching aggressively, which then causes the KV read path to serialize on a smaller pool of SMs for actual reads/writes.

jess: hypothesis: our kernel selector picks the fused flash variant for seq_len > 512 because it reduces compute, but it increases prefetch pressure for KV. for these short-batched workloads the fused variant loses due to KV contention.

nate: quick experiment: override selector to force non-fused variant and replay.

jess: did that locally — p99 dropped back to baseline. diff from trace (non-fused):
```text
flash_attention_nonfused_v1  8.9ms
kv_read_kernel               3.1ms
kv_write_kernel              1.9ms
```

sara: nice. longer-term we should: 1) make selector aware of kv-read fanout and batch-size/seq_len distribution, 2) add per-SM KV cache counters to detect hot slots, 3) tune prefetch stride in fused variant.

jess: opening a perf ticket and a gated canary to test selector change + per-SM kv counters. cc @nate @sara

nate: +1. also add rollout gating: fallback to nonfused if canary shows >5% extra p99.

perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-4123 and canary run 2050012389. /ci/canaries/2050012389

jess: thanks — i'll attach the full microtrace and nvprof exports to PERF-4123 and follow up with kernel-level instrumentation PR.
